section.title: The Last Quiet Hour
section.form_description: A speech meant to move someone to act — the narrator talking Shepard (or whoever is listening) up off the floor and back into the fight. Sections are the rising beats of an address: the stakes named, the doubt named plainly, the evidence from a life lived that it can be done, the call. The narrator's own history is fuel for the exhortation, not the subject of it — but so is the listener's: the narrator holds up the other person's record as often as their own, since it's their record the speech is meant to land on.
section.form_note:
The brief is a speech, not a life story: Jack talking Shepard up in the last hour before the last push, using her own record as proof it can be done. Set after the Cerberus coup, the Citadel DLC shore leave, and the Cronos Station assault, this is the morning of the London conduit assault on Earth — everything is already staged (ships loaded, the plan set, the crew briefed), and the only thing left to do is get up and launch it. Jack is rousing Shepard right before he walks out to fight, not settling him in for the night. Romanced Jack per canon.choices (romance: Jack), consummated per jack_meeting/normandy-engineering scene at the end of ME2, with the Citadel DLC back tattoo. Note: choices.yaml's citadel_coup detail says Thane "died protecting the dalatrass," but the event record (thane-krios-death-defending-the-salarian-councilor) and the coup scene (citadel-coup-csec-office-kai-leng) both have him dying for the Salarian Councilor — treating this as the user's shorthand slip, not a real contradiction, and writing it as the Councilor. Per Thomas's request, "what-cerberus-made-me-for" and "the-kids-at-grissom" were rebuilt off shared Shepard/Jack history and broader lore instead of the Teltin and Grissom backstory events: recruitment off the Purgatory prison ship (jack-recruitment-purgatory) plus the Jack/Miranda confrontation Shepard settled (jack_miranda_dispute: appeased both), and the Suicide Mission itself (Jack held the biotic barrier, all-survived outcome per suicide_mission canon). Pragia/Teltin and Grissom get at most a glancing bridging mention, never the anchor. Jack's framing of "holding a barrier is a focus problem, not a strength problem" and "Cerberus bought a weapon and Shepard made a person" are her own editorializing on the record, not new corpus facts.
Revision per Thomas: Shepard's own AU record is now a load-bearing second thread, not a token mention. Jack is pitching HIM back to himself — every section now carries at least one beat where she cites something true of Shepard specifically as the proof, not just her own Purgatory/barrier/Brimstone/Murtock record. Sourced from config/canon/choices.yaml's Shepard AU overrides (Normandy-born, no parents, gang and drug problem before Anderson pulled him into N7; Sole Survivor of Akuze, the whole squad dead but him; Vanguard, biotic charge into the guns; alignment "Paragon, except against oppressors"; first name Thomas) plus the ME2/ME3 record most relevant to a focus-and-resolve pitch: Cerberus rebuilding him from a corpse via the Lazarus Project (a direct mirror to Jack's own tank), Mordin's death at the Shroud finishing the genophage cure, and Thessia — the one fight where Kai Leng actually got the better of him and walked off with Vendetta, which Jack uses as the counter-example, not the insult. Kai Leng's death at Cronos Station, days earlier in the same push on Cerberus's headquarters, closes the speech as proof the focus she's asking for is already proven, not a new trick.
Second revision per Thomas, correcting two errors: (1) the outline had previously let the closing section cite the Illusive Man's suicide as settled proof Jack could point back to. That confrontation happens on the Citadel, concurrent with or immediately after the London conduit assault itself — part of the endgame this speech is walking Shepard out the door toward, not something resolved before it. It has been cut entirely; Kai Leng's death at Cronos Station (a distinct, already-resolved event from the assault on Cerberus's headquarters, which happened before this morning) carries that closing beat on its own. (2) the whole episode was misdated as the evening before, ending in the two of them going to sleep. It is corrected throughout to the morning of the assault itself: the fleet is already massed, the plan already briefed, nothing left to prepare — Jack is waking Shepard and getting him moving, not tucking him in. No section still ends on rest; every "tonight"/"tomorrow" reference has been changed to "today," "now," or "in the next hour," and "The Last Quiet Night" is renamed "The Last Quiet Hour" to hold the tattoo-and-sentiment beat inside a tense pre-launch hush instead of an evening of repose. The Crucible's final choice and Shepard's fate at the end of it remain deliberately left out: that hasn't happened yet either, and reaching for it would still be narrator omniscience, not something Jack could actually voice this morning.
This does not strain the form. `motivational`'s brief is explicit that "the narrator's own history is fuel for the exhortation, not the subject of it" — and Jack's whole method here is to make Shepard's history do exactly that work on Shepard himself: he's not telling her own story for its own sake, she's holding up his record as the evidence because a room full of only Jack's proof lets him nod along without it landing on him. Spine stays `mixed` — some sections anchor to Jack's own events/scenes, some to Shepard's, most to both at once, which is precisely what a speech that argues from the listener's own life looks like structurally. No change to form.

required_facts.fact: In 2177, an Alliance Marine unit is sent to investigate the settlement at Akuze, a human colony on the outskirts of Systems Alliance space, after all contact is lost with the pioneer team. The unit arrives to find the settlement intact but completely abandoned—no survivors are found. When the unit establishes camp for the night, they are attacked by subterranean thresher maws, creatures the Alliance has never encountered before. The unit is nearly completely slaughtered in the attack, with fifty marines killed and only one known survivor reaching the landing zone alive. If Commander Shepard is that sole survivor, Shepard is permanently marked by the trauma. Years later, Corporal Toombs is discovered to have also survived the attack. Toombs reveals a shocking truth: the massacre was not an accident. According to Toombs' testimony, the renegade black ops group Cerberus deliberately set the thresher maws on the marines as part of an experiment to study the creatures and observe how the unit responded to an unknown threat. Toombs was captured by Cerberus after the attack and subjected to horrific ordeals including being injected with thresher maw acid as part of their research. The revelation that Cerberus orchestrated the massacre haunts Shepard throughout the trilogy, becoming a symbol of Cerberus's willingness to sacrifice human lives for their research agenda.

beats.text: Jack messages that she has more free time, and Shepard invites her up to the apartment.

She brings Eezo, a varren from Thessia she pulled out of a shelter. Exposure to element zero in the Thessian environment left him biotic; biotic varren run short-tempered, which is why they get abused and abandoned. He arrived angry and mistrustful of everyone, and enough patience turned him into, in her words, a big old softy — he plays catch with Shepard.

By 2186 she has grown her hair out and, in her own summary, become dependable, which she blames on Shepard.

evidence.page: Jack (Subject Zero) — Character Analysis (Part 2) — Psyche and Arc
evidence.text: After the Collector Base and Shepard's surrender to the Alliance, Jack is alone again — until the Alliance offers her a teaching post at Grissom Academy training biotic children ("Teltin if it were run by good people"). She becomes the positive figure for kids that she never had. She now wears more clothing and grows her hair out — signs of moving on. When the Alliance wants her students used as biotic artillery, she argues for a defensive, protective support role: the old Jack would have relished commanding destructive biotics; this Jack chooses to protect them. Reunited with Shepard, she says his attitude rubbed off on her, that her students and Shepard are the closest thing to family she has ever had, and grudgingly that "maybe your little suicide squad taught me something about teamwork." During the Reaper War the two are separated again by duty; on shore leave at a bar, doubt briefly reverts her to her old self before Shepard again refuses to leave her. To show her love, she gives Shepard the thing most personal to her — a tattoo. Asked if she has ever tattooed anyone else: "Nobody else mattered enough." She inks a smaller version of her back tattoo on Shepard's right shoulder blade, and confesses the reason: so she can identify him "barely breathing, lying under a pile of rubble at the ass end of this war."

evidence.text:
Citadel: Party was a Mass Effect 3 mission in the Citadel DLC in which Commander Shepard hosted a gathering at the Personal Apartment during shore leave. Joker suggested the party immediately after the attempted hijacking of the Normandy SR-2 in Citadel Docks: Retake the Normandy. To prepare, Shepard bought Party Provisions for 100 credits, or 90 with both Intel Terminal discounts, from a kiosk at the Silver Coast Casino bar, then sent invitations from the apartment's private terminal. The party had to be held before Priority: Cerberus Headquarters, after which the DLC content closed.

Joker, EDI, Liara, James Vega, Steve Cortez, and Samantha Traynor were auto-invited as guaranteed survivors. All other guests were optional and required surviving all three games with their Mass Effect 3 arcs complete: Garrus, Grunt, Jacob, Jack, Javik, Kasumi, Samara, Zaeed, Wrex, Ashley or Kaidan, Tali, and Miranda Lawson, each with specific prerequisites. Squadmates fated to die in their arcs, Legion and Thane Krios, did not appear; Mordin Solus would not break cover even if he survived; Morinth was absent. Other Normandy crew such as Karin Chakwas could not attend, with Traynor stating Chakwas was handling a medical emergency on the Citadel.

Glyph asked Shepard to pick a Quiet or Energetic theme, which set dialogue but not group arrangements. The party ran in phases: an opening, a second part where Shepard could keep or switch the theme and settle guest disagreements, and a final phase whose arrangements followed the second theme, with Shepard choosing which group Glyph joined. Kasumi repeatedly uncloaked to interject. Conversations covered the two Normandys, biotics versus muscle, Joker's refusal to keep a gun in the cockpit, and Miranda and Jack's feuding. The phase ended with a Group Photo, later hung near the downstairs bar, in which romantic couples faced each other.

Shepard woke in the aftermath, potentially beside a love interest; an unromanced female Shepard could wake with James Vega or Javik. If Mordin had survived through the genophage arc, a datapad of his recordings lay by the bed. The guests dispersed around the apartment before Shepard signaled Rapid Transit to return everyone to Docking Bay D24. The Normandy crew gathered at the observation window; if Shepard had romanced Thane, his spirit appeared to speak to his siha before Shepard boarded last, closing the DLC. The Silversun Strip remained accessible afterward. Mark Meer later said Shepard's final franchise line, recorded for this mission, was "The best."

evidence.text:
A collection of Jack dialogue and party-banter clips spanning Mass Effect 2 and Mass Effect 3: a cut Mass Effect 2 conversation about red sand, the Mass Effect 3 scene introducing her varren Eezo, Normandy confrontations with Miranda, her time as an instructor at Grissom Academy leading a biotic student squad, a reunion with Garrus, and the Citadel DLC reconciliation with Miranda. It is useful as voice reference and for Jack's personal continuity. Representative lines:

evidence.text:
The Blue Suns were a "private security organization" that was in reality a ruthless, discreet, and expensive mercenary outfit operating in the Skyllian Verge. Members bore a blue sun tattoo, removed with acid wash during high-risk jobs. The group was mostly batarian, turian, and human, and used YMIR, FENRIS, and LOKI mechs. It was founded in 2160 by Zaeed Massani and Vido Santiago as a protection racket, Zaeed leading the men and Vido handling administration. A dispute over hiring batarians led to a 2165 power struggle in which Vido seized control and nearly killed Zaeed. Vido then hired batarians freely and installed Solem Dal'Serah as the public head of operations while remaining hidden as "Co-Executive Officer."

In Mass Effect: Revelation (2165), the Suns were hired by Edan Had'dah for the Sidon raid; Saren Arterius killed several, including Groto Ib-ba, during his investigation, and Suns under Skarr captured Kahlee Sanders before dying when an element zero refinery was destroyed. In Incursion (2183) a Suns–Collector exchange of humans on Omega was wiped out by Aria T'Loak. In Redemption the Suns recovered Commander Shepard's body from Alchera for the Shadow Broker but were ambushed by Liara T'Soni and Feron. In Foundation the Illusive Man hired Suns as a containment crew during Subject Zero's rampage.

In Mass Effect 2 (2185) Shepard repeatedly clashed with the Suns: they controlled Omega's Gozu District until the plague weakened their non-human members; they besieged Archangel (Garrus Vakarian) alongside Eclipse and Blood Pack under coordinator Tarak, aided by Sidonis's betrayal, and were destroyed with Tarak's gunship. The Suns ran the Purgatory prison under Warden Kuril, who betrayed Shepard during Jack's recruitment and was killed. Suns officer Jedore funded Okeer's krogan project on Korlus and killed him. On Zorya, Zaeed pursued Vido Santiago through a Blue Suns-controlled refinery. Other operations included Harkin's Citadel racket, Prothean dig-site raids on Joab and Kopis, and pirate raids via the MSV Strontium Mule and Sanctum base. In Mass Effect 3 (2186), with Aria's help Shepard secured the allegiance of the Citadel Blue Suns under Darner Vosque, who had been raiding C-Sec weapons shipments and targeting General Septimus Oraka.

evidence.text:
Major Coats was a British Systems Alliance soldier stationed on Earth during the Reaper invasion, serving under the command of Admiral Anderson. Before Hammer's final assault, Coats spent three days holed up inside the Big Ben clock tower in London, firing at anything that moved.

During the final battle on Earth, Coats provided covering fire while Commander Shepard was extracted by a UT-47 Kodiak Drop Shuttle. Admiral Anderson later ordered him to coordinate the artillery strikes that supported Shepard's team as it advanced toward the Citadel beam. After Shepard was hit by Harbinger during the run on the beam, Coats was heard over the radio ordering all surviving soldiers to fall back from the attack.

The aftermath depended on Shepard's choices. If Shepard activated the Crucible, Coats was seen helping rebuild London alongside Gabriella Daniels and Kenneth Donnelly, provided the engineering pair had also survived the war. If Shepard had not brought most of the galaxy's forces into the final battle, Coats was instead shown smoking a cigarette amid London's ruins.

Coats first appeared inside Big Ben in the debut trailer for Mass Effect 3 and again in the "Take Earth Back" trailer, and he referenced his time in the tower in dialogue before Hammer's attack. He was voiced by Nick Boulton, who also voiced Reyes Vidal in Mass Effect: Andromeda and the male Hawke in Dragon Age.

Before ending the meeting, Aria tells them to look in the mining processing plant in Omega's lower levels. Feron's confidence dissolves when the representative turns out to be Tazzik, a salarian of imposing stature and the Broker's personal enforcer. As Tazzik pays off the Blue Suns, Feron attempts to use a nearby turret to disable Tazzik's ship. He misses and destroys a stack of crates, alerting Tazzik as Liara attacks the Blue Suns with biotics. Tazzik flees Omega, Shepard's body having been moved aboard his ship.

evidence.text:
Harbinger was a Reaper that resided in dark space with the rest of the Reaper fleet and was directly responsible for the Collectors' operations in 2185. Its involvement began two months after the Battle of the Citadel, when it made a deal with the Shadow Broker to obtain Commander Shepard's body following the destruction of the SSV Normandy; this failed, and Shepard was resurrected by the Lazarus Project.

In Mass Effect 2, Harbinger was the mastermind behind the Collectors, controlling them through the Collector General as its proxy and directing them to abduct the populations of human colonies to process captives into a Human-Reaper. Harbinger could "assume direct control" of any individual Collector in combat, speaking through it to command troops or threaten enemies; possession made the Collector significantly more powerful but appeared painful, and the body always disintegrated when defeated, an effect likened to Sovereign's possession of Saren Arterius's corpse. Harbinger showed a personal interest in Shepard, repeatedly ordering the Collectors to recover the Commander's body intact. After Shepard's team assaulted the Collector Base and destroyed the incomplete Human-Reaper, and whether the base was destroyed or purged of life, Harbinger declared Shepard's failure to stop the Reapers, relinquished control of the Collector General, and vowed the Reapers would "find another way," then was seen moving with the fleet toward the Milky Way. In the Arrival DLC, Harbinger appeared as a hologram to discuss the futility of Shepard's fight after the Project delayed the Reapers' arrival.

In Mass Effect 3, Harbinger was one of the Reapers leading the attack on Earth, and Alliance intelligence believed it the oldest and largest Reaper in the fleet. It appeared during the final battle in London, launching a devastating attack with unusually fast weapons on forces trying to reach the conduit, and departed when it seemed the counterattack had been wiped out; Shepard and David Anderson nonetheless reached the Citadel, both badly wounded. Harbinger's ultimate fate followed that of the other Reapers depending on Shepard's choice at the Crucible. The Leviathan DLC revealed that Harbinger was the first Reaper created, formed in the image of the Leviathans, and that each 50,000-year harvest directed by the Catalyst ended with the birth of a new Reaper made in Harbinger's image.

evidence.text:
Jack, also known as Subject Zero and Jacqueline Nought (birth name Jennifer), was a notorious human criminal and possibly the most powerful human biotic alive. Born in 2161, she was abducted by Cerberus in 2165, reportedly from Eden Prime, after accidental in-utero element zero exposure gave her biotic potential; her mother was told she had died. She became the central subject of Cerberus' experiment at the Teltin facility on Pragia, which sought to maximize human biotic potential regardless of cost. Every successful enhancement was applied to her; other biotic children were used as expendable test subjects and frequently killed. She was tortured physically and psychologically, kept behind a soundproofed one-way mirror, and forced into gladiatorial fights against the other children, being shocked for hesitating and injected with narcotics for killing, conditioning her to associate killing with euphoria. The other children came to hate her as the source of their suffering.

During a transfer, the subjects rioted, freeing Jack, who flew into a fury and killed nearly everyone in the facility before stealing a shuttle and escaping into the Dakka system. The ship that picked her up used her and sold her as a slave. The Illusive Man shut Teltin down shortly after, later claiming it had "gone rogue." Jack took the name Jack, reacting violently to "Subject Zero," and lived a violent life of piracy, gang membership, vandalism (crashing a space station into a hanar moon), and a stint in a cult (from which she kept her shaved head). In Mass Effect: Foundation she assaulted a Cerberus facility, killed Doctor Angersol, defied the Illusive Man, tried to free biotic student trainees, fought Kai Leng and Rasa, and was knocked out and captured by Blue Suns.

Jack was eventually imprisoned on the Blue Suns prison ship Purgatory, where she was assaulted and raped by guards and prisoners and then murdered every attacker; the Warden kept her in cryostasis until Shepard's team bought her freedom in 2185. Rendered a borderline psychopath but still haunted by her past, she joined Shepard in exchange for her Teltin files, then asked Shepard to help her destroy the abandoned facility with a bomb planted in her old cell (the mission Jack: Subject Zero). There the team encountered Aresh, a fellow test subject trying to restore Teltin; Shepard could stop Jack from killing him. If Miranda's loyalty mission was done, Shepard had to mediate a fight between Jack and Miranda over Cerberus' blame; siding with Miranda cost Jack's loyalty and ended any romance.

Jack was a romance option for a male Shepard. Casual sex ended communication; a slower approach revealed her past, including the partner Murtock who died to save her, leaving her survivor's guilt, and culminated in a tender, emotional love scene. Mordin Solus offered Shepard biotics safety advice. Rejecting her as a "lost cause" made her hostile.

By 2186 (if she survived the Suicide Mission), Jack had grown her hair into a ponytail with shaved sides, matured, and taken a teaching post at Grissom Academy training combat biotics, considering her students the family she never had. During Cerberus' raid to kidnap the students (Grissom Academy: Emergency Evacuation), Jack defended them alongside Shepard and Kahlee Sanders, punching Shepard on reunion for reasons depending on prior choices. She disciplined Ensign Rodriguez and Jason Prangley and led the students in support of Shepard's squad. If Shepard did not arrive in time, Jack appeared as an indoctrinated Phantom at Cronos Station and had to be killed. If romanced, she could rekindle or end the relationship at Purgatory Bar. In the final battle she could be contacted by comm; in a surviving-galaxy ending she is seen gazing at the stars, visiting her students' graves, or alive with her students, depending on choices. If killed, her name appears on the Normandy memorial wall as Jacqueline Nought. In the Citadel DLC she fights in the Armax Arena, introduces her biotic varren Eezo from Thessia, and can tattoo a romanced Shepard so his body can be identified. Jack was voiced by Courtenay Taylor and written primarily by Brian Kindregan.

evidence.text:
Varren were omnivores with a preference for living prey, originally native to the krogan homeworld of Tuchanka. Like most Tuchanka life they were savage, clannish, and durable survivors: pack hunters when prey was easy, scavengers when outmatched. Their adaptability, viciousness, and rapid breeding made them ubiquitous and dangerous pests wherever the krogan traveled, wreaking havoc on native ecologies. The krogan had a millennia-long love-hate relationship with varren, alternately fighting them for territory and raising them as treasured companions and beasts of war; batarians also used them in war. A common silver-scaled subgenus earned the nickname "fishdogs." Varren coloration varied between eras and worlds, from white-bellied dark-backed animals in 2183 to brown-striped varieties by 2185.

Shepard first encountered varren in the Prothean ruins on Feros, where colonists like Davin Reynolds hunted them for meat and Shepard was asked to kill a rabid alpha varren; the animals were vicious enough to attack geth. Batarians deployed "Batarian War Beasts" on Asteroid X57 during Bring Down the Sky, and Simon Atwell noted varren did not always wait for prey to die before eating. On Tuchanka, a tame retired pit champion named Urz stood beside the trader Ratch and would follow Shepard around Clan Urdnot's camp if given pyjak meat. Mordin Solus was seen combating "scale-itch," a varren-borne sexually transmitted disease, aboard the Normandy. Varren were a popular food source, advertised at Illium's "Fishdog Food Shack" and in Citadel ads for "McSorley's Cloaca Margarine." The salarians studied varren (designated "species 408") as potential biological weapons. In the Citadel DLC, Jack noted that varren on Thessia could develop element-zero-fueled biotics, making them more aggressive; she adopted a red-skinned one named Eezo. Besides pit fights, varren were trained for less violent racing. The Andromeda Initiative brought only tissue samples, cloned into edible meat.

evidence.text:
Biotics was the ability of some lifeforms to create mass effect fields using element zero nodules embedded in body tissues, accessed and augmented through bio-amps. Biotic individuals could knock enemies over at range, lift them into the air, generate gravitational vortices to tear apart obstacles or enemies, or create protective barriers. Abilities fell into three categories: telekinesis (mass-lowering fields), kinetic fields (mass-raising fields), and spatial distortion (shifting fields that rip apart objects). Powers were triggered by "physical mnemonics," physical gestures that fired neurons in sequence.

All asari were naturally biotic from birth and required no implants or special training. Biotics of other species were individuals exposed to dust-form element zero in utero who developed eezo nodules throughout their nervous systems. Exposure rarely produced biotics; most exposed fetuses were unaffected, and others developed brain tumors or other complications. In humans, only about one in ten eezo-exposed infants developed usable talent, and in rare cases talents emerged in young adulthood through additional exposure. Identified biotics were typically fitted with a surgically implanted amplifier around puberty and then underwent long biofeedback training.

The first human biotics were born after starship accidents in the 2150s dispersed element zero over populated areas; the first known was female, dubbed "Subject White." Conatix Industries was founded to track exposed individuals and develop implants, and in 2160 established the BAaT programme on Jump Zero, which was shut down after the turian instructor Commander Vyrnnus was killed by a student. Human biotics were classed by implant model: L1, the notorious L2 (introduced 2167, powerful but often unstable and medically damaging), L3 (2170, stable but weaker), retrofit and experimental variants, L4 used in the Ascension Project, and L5x and L5n for Adepts and Vanguards by 2185. Dr. Ellen Ryder created the first human biotic implants. Human biotics faced widespread prejudice, while the Alliance military eagerly recruited them, granting them a 4,500-kilocalorie daily ration.

Among aliens, biotics varied in rarity: common and powerful in asari, rare and prized in salarians, uncommon and distrusted in turians (relegated to Cabals), few but extremely powerful in krogan (Battlemasters such as Skarr and Wrex), and very rare in quarians. Batarians, drell (Thane Krios), Collectors, Protheans (Javik), volus, and vorcha also produced biotics. Non-sapient biotic creatures existed on eezo-rich worlds like Thessia and Eingana, including Jack's biotic varren Eezo. Biotics were exceedingly rare or absent in the Andromeda galaxy.

evidence.text:
Thessia was the asari homeworld, the second planet of the Parnitha System in the Athena Nebula, and the core of the largest economy in the Milky Way. It has been called the "crown jewel of the galaxy," the "apex of democracy," and the "beating heart of galactic love." Its republics had a remarkably low incidence of war, disease, violent crime and famine, supported by wealthy colonies and Thessia's vast element zero reserves, which were large enough to affect the price of eezo galaxy-wide. Traces of element zero in the water and soil were so common that most native life adapted to it, making the world home to many biotically active and eezo-resistant species. Travel to Thessia was strictly controlled, though smuggling persisted.

Rather than a single government, Thessia was host to varying republics, each with a formidable military, and had long been free of internal or external wars. The asari were renowned for cultural and political dominance and excelled at diplomacy, holding a strong presence in Citadel politics. This unfocused political structure left the Thessians unprepared for the Reaper invasion of 2186, which eliminated the communications infrastructure underpinning asari e-democracy and left millions without power, water or food, a deliberate Reaper strategy since husks alone struggled to subdue a population full of biotics. The planet became the setting of the mission Priority: Thessia.

Cultural details include a distinctive fashion sense with non-asari patrons such as Edan Had'dah; food and drink served with small amounts of element zero, prompting a separate visitors' menu, though the drink elasa could be consumed by asari and non-asari alike; and native plants such as the common irssal, a honey-smelling blossom whose seeds were carried by colonists toward the Andromeda galaxy. Thessia lay on the Illium–Thessia shipping lane. The name is adapted from Thessaly, whose "witches" Roman writers said could draw down the moon.

evidence.text: After the rescue from Jon Grissom Academy, Jack can be found on the Citadel in Purgatory Bar after the attempted Cerberus coup reading duty rosters for her kids even while on shore leave. Shepard can either tell her to keep at it, or convince her to lighten up a bit, which colors Jack's responses throughout the conversation. If Shepard thinks Jack fits in snugly to military life, Jack says that their little suicide squad apparently taught her something about teamwork. If the students had been sent to the front lines, Jack mentions her kids are being sent into hot spots for hit\-and\-runs and she's making sure the higher\-ups won't give them something way out of their league. She expresses her surprise at their ability to hold up under fire, but then Shepard believed in the students' abilities and burned away her doubts. If the students had been assigned support roles, she remarks they've been spread out across Alliance units, saving a lot of lives by providing barrier support, modding ammo and the like, and that they're handling the support duties well. If Shepard convinced Jack to take her job seriously, Jack mentions that her kids even saw action on Palaven, either on the front lines with Prangley displaying exceptional biotic aptitude against Cannibals and Rodriguez not panicking for a change, or that her kids provided barriers for a krogan squad so the latter can get close and break enemy lines. They manage to help the turians evac a thousand civilians to safety. Jack suggests fighting would be more fun with Shepard as the Commander finds bigger fights, but claims the "little shits" would be useless without her, and blames Shepard for the perception that she's apparently "dependable" now. If Jack was previously romanced, Shepard has the option to rekindle or officially end their relationship at this time. The Commander asks Jack to dance with them, regardless of whether she was romanced or not, claiming that she's on shore leave and the rosters can wait. Jack flat\-out retorts that everyone knows Shepard can't dance, and with that they both enjoy the music. If Shepard does not help Grissom Academy in time, she will appear as an indoctrinated Phantom when Shepard raids Cerberus Headquarters. An audio log can be found where Jack is heard resisting her captors up until the end. After the squad is forced to kill her, Shepard states that she was no longer herself and that she is "just one more thing Cerberus will answer for." In the final battle on Earth, Shepard can speak with the communications officer in order to call Jack. Jack indicates that she's in the fight but can't reach Shepard's location. If a male Shepard has a romance with Jack, Jack will tell Shepard that he needs to survive, because she is "getting laid" after the war is over. If Shepard chooses to use the Crucible, Jack can be seen gazing at the stars in the future. If Jack didn't have a relationship with Shepard by the time the Commander uses the Crucible, her fate will be determined by the path her students took. She will either be seen visiting her students' graves if they were previously sent to the front lines, or she will be seen with her kids — alive — and Kahlee Sanders mulling their next move if the students were relegated to support. If Jack did not survive Shepard's suicide mission or was killed on Cronos Station, her name will be engraved in the memorial wall on the Normandy as Jacqueline Nought, a pseudonym she used at least once in the past.

evidence.text: “I'm dependable now. I blame you for this, Shepard.” In 2186, provided she survived the Suicide Mission, Jack has altered her appearance, having grown out her hair into a pony tail, but retaining the shaven sides. She now sports a punky studded jacket over a white top that reveals her midriff and its numerous tattoos. She has become more mature, and states that some of Shepard's attitude rubbed off on her. Sometime after the Collectors' defeat, Jack was approached by the Systems Alliance and offered a teaching position at the Grissom Academy to train biotics for combat. She accepted and agreed to tone down her profanity to maintain the level of professionalism expected from teachers. Her students apparently responded well to her unconventional teaching style, mimicking her trash talk ("I will destroy you!") and sticking affectionate appellations like "the psychotic biotic". Jack herself grew attached to her charges in return, considering them the family she never had, and promises to exact retribution against anyone who screws with her kids. Jack is present on the station during Cerberus' attempt to kidnap gifted students for their cause, defending hers from being captured. Shepard finds Jack in the middle of shielding one of her students from incoming Atlas fire, and while Shepard's team takes care of the opposition Jack rallies to her kids on higher ground, helping project a biotic barrier and supporting biotic strikes. Jack's fist lands on Shepard's face the moment the smoke clears, the exact reason why depends on Shepard's previous actions. If a male Shepard romanced her, she hit him for leaving her, then immediately kisses him passionately afterwards. If Shepard expresses misgivings about previously working with Cerberus, Jack cites either handing over the Collector Base to them or the deaths they've caused as her reason. If Shepard merely reminds her how they saved her ass, Jack sarcastically asks if they want a medal. Whichever the case, Shepard's squadmates interject and Jack has some choice replies for some of them. After giving instructions to her students and admonishments to Jason Prangley, Jack relates to Shepard the things she's been up to over the past few months. If the conversation turns into improving the students' endurance and conditioning, Jack specifically recalls her time in the Suicide Mission either throwing husks around or being Shepard's biotic bubble specialist whenever the students complain, telling the kids she kept thinking that she should've let Mordin handle her job instead as he can "talk \[the Collectors] to death." If Mordin died, though, Jack feels bad, recalling the "wicked sex advice" he often gave. Once all the catch\-up is over she stays put until Shepard paves the way for their exit route. One of her students, Ensign Rodriguez, wavers when Cerberus starts messaging the students, and Jack gives the student a dressing\-down. Jack either gives Rodriguez her coarse affirmation of her student's abilities, or shoves the surgery scars inflicted during her Cerberus captivity into her scared student's view, angrily asserting that surrender is tantamount to being meat on a slab. The Ensign sets her head straight after this, and Jack leads the students in shadowing Shepard's team from higher ground while the squad clears out the bulk of Cerberus resistance. Privately, Jack believes her kids aren't yet ready for the realities of war, but Shepard can influence her into letting the students run loose for a while even if they're only fighting from relatively safe positions. Jack, Shepard and Kahlee Sanders eventually manage to help the students escape. Jack, in a good mood, wants to treat her kids to tattoos at the next place they dock. If a male Shepard chose to break with her earlier, Jack even mentions hanging on to the N7 tattoo on her ass she previously planned to burn off. As they make their way back to the Normandy, Jack decides to break her self\-censoring when Joker takes note of the fact and wisecracks that if Jack had a swear jar the cash inside would've been sufficient to buy a cruiser. After the rescue from Jon Grissom Academy, Jack can be found on the Citadel in Purgatory Bar after the attempted Cerberus coup reading duty rosters for her kids even while on shore leave. Shepard can either tell her to keep at it, or convince her to lighten up a bit, which colors Jack's responses throughout the conversation. If the students had been sent to the front lines, Jack mentions her kids are being sent into hot spots for hit\-and\-runs and she's making sure the higher\-ups won't give them something way out of their league.

Aria explained her intention to retake Omega from Cerberus: she had assembled a fleet to break through the Cerberus ships guarding the station, but expected the real fighting to happen on foot through the station. She named the leader of the occupation as Oleg Petrovsky, admitted she had little intelligence on enemy ground forces, but claimed to know exploitable secrets about Omega. She offered Shepard troops and supplies for the Reaper war in exchange for help retaking Omega, on the condition that Shepard come alone, without squadmates, while her forces engaged the bulk of the enemy elsewhere. No morality points were awarded. The skycar dropped Shepard and Bray at a docking bay; Aria left her fleet's coordinates with Bray, urged secrecy while on the Citadel, and Shepard was automatically returned to the Normandy SR-2. The mission was written by Neil Pollner.

evidence.text: Sovereign had possibly planned this for centuries after discovering the Protheans' sabotage plan. Vigil gives Shepard a data file that will give the Commander temporary control of the Citadel to stop Sovereign. After leaving Vigil, Shepard heads through the archives, down into an old aqueduct guarded by geth, and reaches the Conduit. Saren had already gone through, leaving geth to stay guard. Meanwhile, Sovereign begins its assault on the Citadel, escorted by a large geth fleet. Matriarch Lidanya, the commander of the Destiny Ascension, attempts to close the Citadel's arms but the station doesn't respond—the operators at Citadel Control are all dead. The Council are forced to evacuate aboard the Ascension. Saren has begun his attack from within. Back on Ilos, Shepard sees the Conduit is closing fast. Rushing to the Conduit, Shepard evades the geth in the process and drives the Mako through, just before the relay closes. On the Presidium, now burning and heavily damaged, two geth troopers notice a blue glow around the Relay Monument. When they go to take a look, the Mako suddenly bursts through and crushes them, before rolling over and crashing against a wall. The race to stop Saren is on.

evidence.text: During the Reaper War, Harbinger is one of the Reapers who leads the attack on Earth. Alliance intelligence suggests that Harbinger is the oldest and largest Reaper of the entire fleet. Harbinger appears during the final battle in London and launches a devastating attack on allied forces attempting to reach the Citadel through the conduit, using weapons that are considerably faster than other Reapers'. It leaves when it appears that Shepard and the rest of the counterattack have been wiped out. Despite its efforts, Shepard and David Anderson make it through, though they are both heavily wounded. If Shepard chooses to activate the Crucible, Harbinger's fate is presumably the same as the other Reapers'. It is either destroyed with all other synthetic life, brought under Shepard's control and used to rebuild and protect the galaxy, or it willingly helps to rebuild the galaxy and disseminate its knowledge after organic and synthetic life are merged. If Shepard refuses to activate the Crucible, then Harbinger is presumably defeated along with the other Reapers in a future cycle.

evidence.text:
Short lore page. The Conduit of Mass Effect 3 was a massive structure the Reapers built in war-torn London in 2186 to transport corpses and other matter directly from the ground to the Citadel, which had been relocated above Earth. Allied galactic forces called it a "conduit" and attempted to storm it in order to reopen the arms of the Citadel for the next stage of the war, but were largely annihilated by Harbinger; only Commander Shepard and David Anderson reached the Citadel.

The structure followed basic mass relay principles but differed in several ways: it emitted a constant beam of blue light into the sky rather than lighting up only during transmission, had no visible element zero core, allowed living matter to survive the trip unaided (arriving at ballistic but survivable speeds), and appeared to have multiple destination termini, since Shepard and Anderson materialized at slightly different points on the station. In some outcomes of Shepard's final decision, the conduit appeared to have been remodeled or rebuilt using prevailing galactic architecture.

evidence.text: When Taetrus fell, the turians knew little about the Reapers except that they wanted to enrage the turians. Staying calm, the turians massed in force around Palaven, their homeworld. Fleet Admiral Irix Coronati, in what became known as the "Fifteen\-Minute Plan," stationed only two carriers, Undaunted and Resolute, near the system's relay. When the Reaper fleet emerged, the carriers launched swarms of unmanned fighters and spy drones. These were quickly destroyed, but the drones transmitted vital data on the Reapers' effective range, fleet composition, and exact location. The turians' other ships then deployed to defend the system in earnest. Knowing that the Reapers' weapons had a longer effective range than any of his own, Coronati made a short, daring FTL jump\-\-landing his dreadnoughts in the middle of the Reaper fleet. The dreadnoughts then turned to line up their main guns on the Reapers, which also needed to turn to fire on the turians. This ploy used the Reapers' size against them\-\-because they could turn faster, the turian dreadnoughts locked targets first, and their concentrated firepower downed several Reaper capital ships. The Reapers countered instantly. Their destroyers performed a jump of their own to the skies above Palaven, beginning orbital strikes on turian cities. The turians, forced to defend the planet, found themselves in a pitched battle far from the relay, from which emerged a seemingly endless line of Reaper ships. After massive casualties, Coronati ordered retreat. The turians insist that Palaven is not lost\-\-the battle has merely moved to the ground. Reaper troop transports have dumped hordes of husks to capture Palaven's inhabitants, but met with little success. Reaper capital ships are destroying city after city. But much of the turian fleet is still operable, and the citizenry is heavily armed. The turians refuse to be intimidated.

evidence.text:
"Race Against Time: Conduit" was the Mass Effect mission that followed "Ilos: Find the Conduit," into which the earlier "Race Against Time: Sovereign" journal entry was renamed. Vigil had revealed that the Conduit was not a weapon but a miniature mass relay serving as a back door onto the Citadel, itself an enormous mass relay. Saren Arterius intended to use the Conduit to reach the Citadel, unlock the station for Sovereign, and trigger a Reaper invasion that would destroy all organic life in the galaxy.

The mission was a linear drive in the Mako out of Vigil's chamber and down a path now cleared of the forcefields that had blocked it earlier. Shepard's squadmates remarked that even the Protheans, with all their power and knowledge, had fallen for the Reapers' traps, and vowed not to share their fate. Geth Rocket Troopers guarded the entrance to a long trench run, which was defended by numerous geth including Rocket Troopers, Troopers, a Shock Trooper, and a Geth Colossus, followed by further groups of Rocket Troopers. There were no item pickups during the driving sections, and the game would not allow Shepard to enter the aqueducts or the Conduit itself without the Mako; entering the Conduit on foot meant instant death.

At the end of the aqueduct the Mako halted at a ledge overlooking the distant Conduit, and a lengthy cutscene showed the Battle of the Citadel beginning: Sovereign and its geth allies arrived through the mass relay and fired a devastating broadside on the Citadel Fleet, the Citadel forces failed to seal the station's arms, and the commander of the Destiny Ascension ordered the Council evacuated. On the Presidium, a geth threw aside the body of an asari as Saren and his minions took the elevator toward the Council Chambers. Regaining control, Shepard had only 40 seconds to reach the Conduit while dodging four Geth Colossi, then drove into the Conduit, which automatically transported the Mako to the Citadel. The mission led directly into "Race Against Time: Final Battle."

evidence.text:
Priority: Earth was the final mission of Mass Effect 3 and the conclusion of Commander Shepard's trilogy. It was acquired after Priority: Cerberus Headquarters; from that point Sol was the only reachable system, and merely traveling there triggered the mission with no way to back out. Allied fleets assaulted the Reapers above Earth while Hammer, the ground force, tried to land troops near the Citadel transport beam.

The mission had two main stages. First, Shepard's shuttle landed to knock out a Reaper anti-aircraft "Hades Cannon" so Hammer could land; the team fought through streets and a ruined house full of Cannibals, Marauders, and Brutes to a crashed assault team, recovered two M-920 Cain shots to destroy the cannon, held off a Banshee (named "Morinth" if that character survived Mass Effect 2) and endless Cannibals, and were extracted, reuniting with Anderson and meeting Major Coats. At the Forward Operating Base, Shepard held final conversations with surviving squadmates, allies, and leaders (Victus, Wrex or Wreav, Kirrahe, and others depending on prior choices) before Anderson gave the battle plan: a frontal armored assault on the conduit past a Reaper Destroyer.

The second stage advanced through occupied London to a missile battery, where Thanix missiles were coordinated with EDI on the Normandy to destroy the Destroyer while the team fought Brutes, Banshees, and a Harvester and dodged the Reaper's beam. Anderson then arrived by APC for the final push, but Harbinger descended on the conduit and annihilated the ground forces. In the Extended Cut, squadmates survived or died based on Effective Military Strength (below 4200 EMS in Legendary Edition they died). A wounded, solitary Shepard fought through Husks and a Marauder with an infinite-clip pistol to reach the beam.

On the reconfigured Citadel, Shepard reunited by comm with Anderson and found him held hostage by a transformed Illusive Man, who could now control both of them. The confrontation's outcome hinged on the final choice, with full Paragon/Renegade options requiring Paragon/Renegade choices at every prior meeting with the Illusive Man. Paragon made him realize he was indoctrinated and shoot himself; Renegade interrupts let Shepard kill him. Shepard then opened the Citadel arms to let the Crucible dock. The Catalyst appeared and offered Destruction, Control, or Synthesis (Refusal was also possible), with availability and galactic damage set by EMS. Every activated ending crippled the Normandy, and its crew's survival, the epilogue scenes, and the placing of Shepard's name plaque above Anderson's on the memorial wall all depended on EMS and prior choices. After the credits a Stargazer told a child tales of "the Shepard."

evidence.text: Sometime prior to the Reaper invasion in 2186, Hackett has attained the rank of Fleet Admiral. He is alerted to the incoming Reaper fleet as several deep\-space outposts go dark and begins mobilizing the Alliance Navy. Unfortunately, the Reapers proved too powerful, forcing Hackett to sacrifice the Second Fleet to allow the Third and Fifth to escape, and also resulting in him presiding over the "worst military defeat in human history." He advises Shepard, reinstated into the Alliance military, to go to Mars, where Liara was researching what appeared to be a Prothean superweapon. Hackett regularly appears via the quantum entanglement video communication device to debrief Shepard after missions throughout the war. Following Shepard's errand to the salarian homeworld Sur'Kesh to retrieve a krogan female, Hackett informs the Commander that construction of the Prothean weapon has begun, dubbed "Project Crucible", describing it as one of the most ambitious undertakings in human history. Hackett and the bulk of what remains of the Alliance fleets guard and oversee construction of the weapon at an undisclosed location. After the battle for Rannoch, Shepard can ask Hackett the reason for being put in charge of combating the Reapers. Hackett explains it's because Shepard has a loyal crew who followed the Commander against Sovereign and survived the Omega 4 Relay, centrally because they believed in Shepard. Hackett expresses his distaste at the Illusive Man's aim to control the Reapers, asserting that he is "trying to tame a shark" and that the whole galaxy could end up paying for his misguided intent. He orders the Commander to kill him. During the assault on Cronos station, Hackett mobilizes the Fifth Fleet against the Cerberus Fleet. He maintains contact with Shepard's team as they fight their way through the station. Later, when Shepard commits the galaxy's combined forces to deploying the Crucible in Sol against the Reapers, he requests clearance to board the Commander's ship. There, he signals the various fleets to mobilize, giving his pre\-battle address to all the soldiers participating in the upcoming fight: *“Never before have so many come together\-\-from all quarters of the galaxy. But never before have we faced an enemy such as this. The Reapers will show us no mercy. We must give them no quarter. They will terrorize our populations. We must stand fast in the face of that terror. They will advance until our last city falls, but we will not fall. We will prevail. Each of us will be defined by our actions in the coming battle. Stand fast. Stand strong. Stand together. Hackett out.”* Afterwards, Shepard and Hackett meet in holo\-conference with Anderson, who reports that the Reapers had moved the Citadel above Earth and had closed the Ward arms, making it impossible for the Crucible to dock. Hackett then details the plan for Sword fleet to engage the Reapers while Hammer strike teams aid the Earth resistance in reaching the conduit in London to teleport to the Citadel and unlock the Ward arms. The assembled fleets launch the all\-out assault on Earth while Hackett and Shield fleet hang back to protect the Crucible, escorting it to the Citadel sometime during the heat of the fighting. Arriving in Earth's orbit, Hackett is informed that Shepard made it to the Citadel and orders all allied ships to defend the Crucible. However, when the Crucible successfully docks with the Citadel, the device fails to work immediately and Hackett loses all contact with Shepard. Following Shepard's activation of the Crucible during the battle for Earth, Hackett orders the fleets to retreat to a predesignated rendezvous point before the Crucible fires. If Shepard intended to destroy the Reapers and there are enough assets gathered for the final fight, Hackett relates how the Reapers were defeated. Even though the galaxy is devastated and the mass relays are severely damaged, Hackett is confident they can rebuild, but regrets that so many people will not be able to witness the future that Shepard made possible. If the Reapers were destroyed but Shepard didn't obtain enough forces, Hackett is left to mull the aftermath as he's marooned aboard his disabled dreadnought in Earth's orbit. The victory was Pyrrhic, and it is up to the survivors to rebuild and start again, though Hackett hopes the lessons learned from this war won't die along with the people who fought to win it.

evidence.text: The next confrontation between Shepard and Saren occurs on the lost Prothean world of Ilos, where the Conduit is hidden. While Shepard is delayed by the Council, which believes a blockade would stop Saren from attacking the Citadel, Saren is able to reach Ilos first. The activated Conduit allows Saren to travel to the Citadel, bypassing its external defenses, while Sovereign and a geth fleet assault the Citadel from the outside. After killing the operators of Citadel Control, Saren makes his way toward the Citadel's master control unit, intending to transfer control of the Citadel to Sovereign to activate the latent mass relay, paving the way for the rest of the Reapers to enter through from dark space. Saren is interrupted, however, when Shepard and the Ilos ground team rush in, following Saren through the Conduit. Shepard can convince Saren that, indoctrinated or not, he still has a way to stop Sovereign. Saren commits suicide by shooting himself in the head, to prevent himself from opening the Citadel relay, but not before muttering, "Goodbye, Shepard. Thank you." Otherwise, Shepard is forced to battle Saren atop the Council platform. At the end of the fight, Saren falls through the glass floor of the Council Chambers and is fatally impaled by a large glass shard. Shepard's team assures Saren's death by shooting the rogue Spectre in the head. Sovereign, however, reanimates the misguided turian's body, burning away all of Saren's flesh, revealing the extent of the cybernetic "upgrades". By controlling Saren's corpse and speaking in his voice, Sovereign has the turian fight one last battle. Shepard and the team manage to destroy the nightmarish construct, and Saren's synthetic remains disintegrate. The avatar's destruction corrupts the signal used by Sovereign to control Saren's body and causes it to lose control of its shields, allowing the Alliance fleet to destroy it. Despite the victory, Shepard knows that fundamentally, Saren was right. Sooner or later the Reapers will return, and Shepard vows to find some way to stop them. |  | ***“Salvation comes with a cost.”*** — Spoilers for **Mass Effect: Ascension** follow. |  | | --- | --- | --- |

evidence.text:
The Citadel Fleet was the main space defense force of the Citadel, made up of turian, salarian, and asari vessels, predominantly turian because of the turians' peacekeeping role. Its flagship was the asari dreadnought Destiny Ascension, the most powerful ship of the Council races. Its exact size was unknown, but it was large enough to patrol every mass relay linking Citadel space to the Terminus Systems while still keeping a force at the Citadel; Ambassador Udina claimed it could secure the entire Attican Traverse if the Council wished.

During the Battle of the Citadel, after the events on Virmire, the Council deployed the fleet to the relays believing Saren Arterius would not dare attack the Citadel directly. The dreadnought Sovereign and a geth fleet then launched a surprise assault. The Destiny Ascension ordered the Wards closed to fortify the station, but Saren had already used the Conduit to infiltrate the Citadel and shut down the station and the relay network, isolating the diminished fleet and blocking reinforcements. Sovereign broke through as the Wards closed behind it. The Council was evacuated to the Destiny Ascension, which could not fight clear of the geth ships. After Shepard reactivated the relays, letting the Alliance Navy and the Normandy arrive, Shepard chose whether to send the reinforcements to save the Council and the Destiny Ascension or to let them fall.

If the Council was saved, the Destiny Ascension survived and later made a 20-colony victory cruise; the turians lost 20 cruisers of 300 crew each, and the Alliance lost eight cruisers and 2,400 personnel. If the Council was left to die, most of the defending fleet was believed destroyed, and Khalisah al-Jilani cited 10,000 dead. Galactic News in 2185 reported plans for an Allied Citadel Defense Unit to replace the fleet, with the Systems Alliance supplying most ships, the Asari Republics ceding defense responsibility to the Turian Hierarchy, and the Hierarchy announcing it would no longer cap its dreadnought production. In 2185 the Citadel Fleet's 24th Fighter Group received the Galactic Unit Citation for being the first unit to engage Sovereign.

evidence.text: *Main article: Sovereign* The first living Reaper to be witnessed by any living intelligent being after the Protheans became extinct was designated Sovereign by the organic races. It is a colossal dreadnought, several times the size of any known vessel – even dwarfing the massive asari flagship, Destiny Ascension. It was first discovered on the edges of geth space in the Perseus Veil by Edan Had'dah's survey teams and studied by Dr. Shu Qian. Saren Arterius, using the doctor's notes stolen sometime in 2165 CE, eventually finds it for himself. At first, it was presumed to be Saren's flagship by those who encountered it; Sovereign did act as transport for the rogue Spectre and his minions. However, Commander Shepard later discovers that Sovereign and its brethren are actually the masterminds behind the Prothean genocide. It acts as the Reapers' vanguard and was originally intended to initiate the next harvest of the galaxy. When Sovereign decided it was time to begin the cycle again, the keepers ignored the order. This greatly complicated matters for Sovereign. In order to unleash its brethren from dark space, it would have to find a way to manually activate the relay from inside the Citadel. While Reapers are undoubtedly beings of terrible power and ferocity, a single Reaper would not be able to survive the combined might of the assembled Citadel races in a direct assault. At some point Sovereign became aware of the Conduit and swayed a significant number of geth into worshiping it. It used Saren to comprehend the Conduit's location from Prothean Beacons while putting its geth in a supporting military capacity. Successful in both regards, in 2183 CE the Reaper marshals its forces and launches an all\-out assault on the Citadel while Saren infiltrates the Citadel through the Conduit. Fortunately, Saren is stopped by Commander Shepard and company, and Sovereign is destroyed by the Alliance Fleet, though this would only forestall the Reaper invasion for a few years. Shepard knows the Reaper fleet, though dormant and hibernating, is still out in dark space and vows to find some way to stop them.

evidence.text: Six months have passed since the destruction of Bahak and Commander Shepard's voluntary return to the Alliance. The Commander has been relieved of command and detained in a Systems Alliance facility in the city of Vancouver on Earth. Without warning, Alliance deep space outposts beyond Sol begin to go dark. Admiral Steven Hackett, the head of the Alliance military, begins to prepare for an imminent invasion. Admiral David Anderson arrives in Vancouver and escorts Commander Shepard with Lieutenant James Vega to a meeting with an Alliance defense committee. Shepard confirms their worst fears: the Reapers have returned to the galaxy and are on their way to Earth. At that moment, contact is lost with Luna Base and news reports begin to surface of an unknown alien force landing in Earth's cities. The Reapers have already arrived. A Reaper capital ship then descends through the clouds over Vancouver and blasts the Alliance building, killing the defense committee and Alliance staff. Shepard and Anderson survive and contact Ashley Williams or Kaidan Alenko (whichever survived Virmire), telling them to get to the Normandy. As Shepard and Anderson make their way from building to building to get to the spaceport, Anderson tells Shepard that they have to get to the Citadel and seek help from the Council. They reach a comm set near a crashed gunship and hail the Normandy to evacuate. After holding off an attack from Cannibals, the Normandy bombs the area clear of attackers. As Shepard boards the ship, Anderson informs the Commander that he will stay behind to lead the resistance, and hands over Shepard's dog tags. Shepard protests, but Anderson charges Shepard with getting as much help as possible to save Earth and stop the Reapers. As the Normandy lifts off, Shepard witnesses a child running to an Alliance evacuation area and boarding a shuttle. As the shuttles lift off, a Reaper destroyer emerges from behind a cluster of buildings and targets the shuttles, killing those who were aboard including the child. Distraught, Shepard steps away from the open shuttle bay doors of the Normandy, and the ship escapes Earth as more Reapers and the wreckage of Alliance ships rain down upon the planet.

evidence.text:
Prologue: Find the Beacon is the opening mission of Mass Effect, acquired after reporting to the Normandy comm room. The SSV Normandy jumps through the Arcturus Prime relay toward Eden Prime, an Alliance colony under attack. Joker runs a system check while the turian Spectre Nihlus observes; Joker dislikes having a Spectre aboard. In the comm room, Nihlus and Captain Anderson reveal the mission is more than a shakedown run: a science team on Eden Prime discovered a Prothean beacon that must be secured and brought to the Citadel, and Nihlus is evaluating Shepard's Spectre potential. A garbled transmission from marines on Eden Prime shows heavy fighting and an immense alien ship. Anderson orders the team down; Nihlus scouts ahead alone.

On the surface, Shepard's squad advances toward the dig site. Corporal Jenkins is killed by Geth Recon Drones. The squad fights through more drones and encounters husks impaled colonists on dragon's teeth spikes. They rescue Gunnery Chief Ashley Williams of the 212, who joins the squad. The beacon has been moved from the dig site to the spaceport. In a cutscene, Nihlus is ambushed and shot dead by fellow turian Saren Arterius. The squad meets farmers led by Cole (who can name a smuggling contact, "Powell") and dockworker Powell near Nihlus's body. Fighting through geth troopers, shock troopers, and a Geth Destroyer, Shepard boards a tram to Spaceport Platform Two, where Saren orders the colony destroyed and is lifted by the beacon. Shepard disarms four explosive charges under a five-minute timer.

Kaidan and Ashley investigate the beacon; it activates and pulls one squadmate toward it. Shepard throws them clear and is lifted instead, receiving chaotic visions before the beacon explodes, knocking Shepard unconscious. Aboard the enemy ship, an asari in black informs Saren that Anderson's team foiled the colony's destruction and that a human may have used the beacon; Saren flies into a rage and orders the human eliminated. Shepard wakes in the Normandy med bay under Dr. Chakwas's care, briefs Anderson, and is ordered to take the ship to the Citadel. Enemies include Geth Destroyers, Recon Drones, Shock Troopers, Snipers, Troopers, and Husks.

evidence.text:
Commander Shepard was the customizable player protagonist of Mass Effect, Mass Effect 2, and Mass Effect 3, born April 11, 2154, a graduate of the Systems Alliance N7 program (service number 5923-AC-2826), a Skyllian Blitz veteran, and a biotic after secondary element zero exposure in 2168. Character creation ("Profile Reconstruction") set gender, appearance, first name (John or Jane by default), class (Soldier, Engineer, Adept, Infiltrator, Sentinel, Vanguard), a pre-service history (Spacer, Earthborn, Colonist), and a psychological profile (Sole Survivor of Akuze, War Hero of Elysium and recipient of the Star of Terra, or Ruthless at Torfan). These choices affected dialogue, bonus Paragon/Renegade points, and access to certain assignments; the stock Shepard was an Earthborn Sole Survivor Soldier. A Spacer Shepard could speak with mother Hannah Shepard.

In 2183 Shepard served as Executive Officer aboard the SSV Normandy under Captain David Anderson and was considered as humanity's first Spectre candidate. In Mass Effect 2, the Normandy was destroyed by an unidentified ship; Shepard died recovering Joker, was retrieved by Feron and Liara T'Soni, and was rebuilt over two years by Cerberus's Lazarus Project under the Illusive Man, then agreed to investigate human colony abductions by the Collectors. Facial scars glowed and shifted with Renegade choices unless surgically healed. In Mass Effect 3 (2186), Shepard, under Alliance arrest for working with Cerberus and the Bahak system's destruction, was reinstated by Anderson when the Reapers attacked Earth, and worked to unite the galaxy and build the Crucible while opposing the Illusive Man. Wounded by Harbinger in the final battle, Shepard reached the Citadel and met the Catalyst, who offered endings: Destroy (kills all synthetics including the geth and EDI), Control (uploads Shepard's mind as Reaper master), Synthesis (merges organic and synthetic life), or Refusal (the cycle continues). If the Crucible fired, Shepard became a legend remembered as "The Shepard," with a closest squadmate placing Shepard's name on the memorial wall. The page also noted the character was named after astronaut Alan Bartlett Shepard Jr., voiced by Mark Meer and Jennifer Hale, and detailed cut ideas such as Shepard being a hidden alien or a visible cyborg.

evidence.text:
Captain David Edward Anderson was a human war hero, born June 8, 2137 in London to Ursula and Paul Anderson. He was the first graduate of the Alliance's N7 Special Forces program and served with distinction in the First Contact War. In Mass Effect: Revelation (2165), then-Lieutenant Anderson, XO of the SSV Hastings, led the ground team responding to the attack on the Sidon research station, discovered it had harbored a traitor secretly researching AI, and was tasked by Ambassador Anita Goyle to investigate discreetly. He tracked down Kahlee Sanders, daughter of Jon Grissom, protected her from the krogan Skarr, and repeatedly clashed with the turian Spectre Saren Arterius. Saren's destruction of an element zero refinery during the rescue killed many civilians; Saren blamed Anderson, which kept Anderson out of the Spectres. Anderson and Kahlee developed a lasting romance.

In the comic He Who Laughs Best, Anderson observed the SSV Normandy's test flight at Arcturus Station and agreed to make Jeff "Joker" Moreau the ship's pilot after Joker hijacked it. In Mass Effect, Anderson, now a Captain and former commander of the SSV Tokyo, was given command of the Normandy and hand-picked Commander Shepard as his XO and protégé. After the Eden Prime mission and Nihlus Kryik's murder by Saren, Anderson supported Shepard's investigation, stepped down as captain to make Shepard a Spectre, and helped Shepard steal the Normandy to reach Ilos, being either shot in the leg by C-Sec or punching Udina unconscious. After Sovereign's destruction he could be endorsed as the human Council representative.

In Mass Effect 2 Anderson had either joined the Council or become an Admiral advising Councilor Udina; he arranged to restore Shepard's Spectre status and admitted stationing Ashley or Kaidan on Horizon. In the novels Ascension, Retribution, Deception, and Conviction, Anderson continued working with Kahlee Sanders against Cerberus, pursued the Reaper-enslaved Paul Grayson, fought Kai Leng, and recruited James Vega on Omega to guard the imprisoned Shepard.

In Mass Effect 3 (2186), Anderson escorted Shepard to the Defense Committee as the Reaper invasion began, then stayed on Earth to lead the human resistance, reinstating Shepard into the Alliance with new dogtags. He coordinated with Shepard by quantum communicator throughout the war. Reuniting in London for the final assault, Anderson and Shepard reached the Citadel's Control chamber, where the indoctrinated Illusive Man forced Shepard to shoot Anderson. Anderson died of his wound beside Shepard, calling it an honor to have fought beside his greatest protégé; his name was added to the Normandy's memorial wall. In Mass Effect: Andromeda, the first human child born in Andromeda could be named David Edward after him.

evidence.text:
In Mass Effect 2, Commander Shepard's armor could be customized by swapping pieces of the default N7 Armor for parts purchased from merchants or supplied through downloadable content, using the Armor Locker aboard the Normandy SR-2. Besides changing physical appearance, each piece affected Shepard's combat effectiveness, and the player could further alter color, reflectiveness, or pattern. Because money was limited, the page recommended buying selectively and always using vendor discounts; purchasing every armor piece with all discounts cost 54,996 credits, or 66,000 without. In Mass Effect Legendary Edition, formerly DLC-exclusive equipment had to be bought with credits and resources or researched in the Normandy Tech Lab rather than being granted automatically.

Customizable slots were head, chest, shoulders, arms, and legs, each with an N7 default piece and several alternatives. Head options included the N7 Helmet and Breather Helmet, Kuwashii Visor, Death Mask, Umbra Visor, Recon Hood, Sentry Interface, Archon Visor, Capacitor Helmet, and Kestrel Helmet, with effects ranging from bonus health and headshot damage to reduced power recharge time. Chest, shoulder, arm, and leg pieces came from manufacturers such as Kassa Fabrication, Armax Arsenal, Rosenkov Materials, Elanus Risk Control Services, Aldrin Labs, and the Sirta Foundation, granting bonuses to health, shields, power damage, weapon damage, melee damage, or ammo capacity. The Kestrel set pieces, from the Aegis Pack, provided combined multi-stat bonuses.

Full armor sets could also be equipped; these could not have individual pieces swapped but offered unique bonus combinations. Shepard could additionally choose casual outfits worn aboard the Normandy and on discreet missions, including outfits obtained through Kasumi - Stolen Memory. Documented bugs included the Archon Visor conferring no benefit in the original release, fixed in Legendary Edition.

evidence.text:
Thresher maws were enormous subterranean carnivores that spent their lives eating or hunting for food, bursting from the ground without warning when disturbed. They reproduced via spores that could lie dormant for millennia and survive deep space and atmospheric re-entry, so maw spores appeared on many worlds, spread by earlier generations of space travelers, possibly predating the asari.

They lived alone in large underground nests, growing over 30 meters above ground with a body nearly twice that size beneath the surface; an adult's body never fully left the ground, with only the head and tentacles erupting to attack. They fed through an unusual photosynthesis using absorbed solar radiation plus minerals and ores consumed from the ground, favoring bodies with little or no atmosphere. Mostly immobile above ground, they moved at high speed while burrowing, absorbed tremendous damage, and attacked by spitting viscous acid, bursting up beneath prey, and smashing targets with their claws while emitting infrasound. Shields were completely ineffective against them.

The Alliance first encountered thresher maws on the colony of Akuze in 2177, where they killed nearly an entire marine rescue force. If Shepard has the Sole Survivor background, Shepard alone survived; Corporal Toombs, met later on Ontarom, claimed Cerberus deliberately caused the Akuze massacre to study the maws and held him captive for experiments, and Cerberus later used the same tactic to lure Admiral Kahoku's team into a nest on Edolus. Maws are found on many uncharted worlds, usually one per planet, including Antibaar, Chohe, Nepheron, Nonuel, Presrop, Xawin, Trebin and Edolus.

In Mass Effect 2, a thresher maw is the final test of Clan Urdnot's Rite of Passage on Tuchanka, lured to the proving grounds by ground-pounding pistons to attack Grunt's krantt. Gatatog Uvenk notes that the last krogan to kill a maw on foot was Urdnot Wrex. In Mass Effect 3, Kalros, a legendary maw called "the mother from which all other thresher maws spawn" and the largest ever seen, roams Tuchanka near the Shroud facility. Shepard activates two maw hammers to summon her against a Reaper Destroyer guarding the Shroud; she coils around it and drags it underground. Her size prompts Javik to remark that maws are now too big to ride, implying they were smaller in Prothean times. The concept was confirmed by art director Derek Watts to draw on Dune's sandworms, and also resembles D&D Ankhegs, the Star Wars Sarlacc, and the real Bobbit worm.

evidence.text:
Corporal Toombs was one of the Alliance marines at Akuze and a survivor of the thresher maw tragedy there. Cerberus had set the thresher maws on his unit as an experiment; when Toombs was found alive afterward, Cerberus was delighted and hauled him off for further study, subjecting him to horrific ordeals over years, including injection with thresher maw acid.

Toombs eventually escaped confinement and, deeply traumatized, began systematically hunting the scientists responsible, hiring mercenary help. If Commander Shepard investigated a series of dead Alliance scientists, they crossed paths with Toombs on Ontarom as he was about to kill the last one, Dr. Wayne. Shepard could talk him down by promising a public trial for Wayne and psychological treatment for Toombs; allow Toombs his revenge; kill Wayne personally under Spectre authority; or shoot Toombs to save the scientist, then send the Fifth Fleet to take Wayne for trial. If Shepard had the Sole Survivor background and spared Wayne while stopping Toombs, Toombs noted that the vids said Shepard was the only one to escape Akuze, said "who am I to argue?" and killed himself.

If Toombs survived the 2183 encounter, he sent Shepard a message in 2185 titled "What the hell?" after learning of Shepard's ties to Cerberus, feeling betrayed and promising retribution: "I've got my own merc team now, Shepard. And I kill any Cerberus team I can find. If I run into you, don't expect any different." Galactic News reports could describe his activities: if both he and Wayne survived, an independent inquiry against Cerberus proceeded on their testimony; if Wayne died, the inquiry dismissed Toombs' claims as those of a disturbed man lacking evidence.

evidence.text:
Akuze was a human colony on the outskirts of Systems Alliance space. In 2177, while Akuze was still in the early stages of colonization, all contact was lost with the pioneer team. An Alliance Marine unit sent to investigate found the settlement intact but no survivors. When the unit camped for the night, it was attacked by thresher maws. Fifty marines were lost and only one reached the landing zone alive.

In Mass Effect, if Commander Shepard was the sole known survivor, C-Sec officer Eddie Lang on the Citadel mentioned a monument at Akuze with a section dedicated to Shepard. Shepard could later learn of a second survivor, Corporal Toombs, who claimed the slaughter was not an accident: he said the black ops group Cerberus had deliberately set the thresher maws on the marines to study the creatures and observe how the unit reacted.

In Mass Effect 2, a survivor Shepard could see news of a Shepard Memorial being erected on Akuze, with a commemoration ceremony hosted by Admiral Steven Hackett planned for 2186 once the site was cleared of thresher maws. If Shepard had rescued Toombs in 2183, he sent a threatening message about Shepard's new alliance with Cerberus. During Lair of the Shadow Broker, after Shepard and Liara defeated Tela Vasir, the asari Spectre cited the Akuze massacre as evidence of Shepard's hypocrisy in allying with Cerberus, the group responsible for those deaths. In Mass Effect 3, a survivor Shepard could view a recording on Cronos Station of a Cerberus scientist and the Illusive Man confirming that Cerberus was behind the attack.

evidence.text: Admiral Hackett resumes contact with Shepard in 2185, but not before becoming involved with planning a memorial for the Commander, who is presumed dead since the attack on the SSV Normandy in 2183\. If Shepard repelled the Skyllian Blitz on Elysium, then on Hackett's orders, all proceeds from weddings held at Shepard Memorial Plaza on Elysium go to benefit the families of veterans and Alliance service members who were killed in action. If Shepard fought on Torfan, Hackett personally orders no arrests be made against those who tried to extinguish the Shepard Memorial Flame on Torfan. If Shepard survived the Thresher Maw attack on Akuze, then the Admiral will be scheduled to preside over the unveiling of the Shepard Memorial on that world in 2186\. The Admiral also transmits to Shepard the location of the Normandy SR\-1 crash site and requests that Shepard place a monument there after recovering the dog tags of fallen crew members. After Liara T'Soni's confrontation with the Shadow Broker, if Shepard did not pursue a romance with Liara, she mentions that Hackett recovered Shepard's dog tags and passed them on to her so that she could return them to their rightful owner.
